div.head: Ine 6.2
div.ab: Gif hwa on ealdormonnes huse gefeohte oððe on oðres geðungenes witan, LX scill. gebete he ⁊ oþer LX geselle to wite.
Gif . . . ðe on oðres geþung . . . . . scill' gebete ⁊ oðer LX . . .
Gif hwa on ealdermonnes huse oððe on oþres witan geþungenan gefeohte, LX scll' gebete he ⁊ oþer LX to wite.
Gyf hwá in ealdormannes huse feohte oððe on oðres geðungenes witan, syxtig scill' gebete hé ⁊ oðer syxtig gesylle he to wite.
Si quis in domo aldermanni uel alterius sagibaronis pugnet, LX sol. emendet et alios LX emendet pro wita.
Gif hwa on ealdormonnes huse gefeohte oððe on oðres geðungenes witan, LX scill. gebete he ⁊ oþer LX geselle to wite.
Gif hwa on ealdormonnes huse gefeohte oððe on oðres geðungenes witan, LX sciƚƚ gebete he ⁊ oþer LX geselle to wite.
Wenn jemand im Hause eines Ealdorman oder in [dem] eines anderen ausgezeichneten Notabeln ficht, büsse er [ihm] 60 Schill. und zahle zweite 60 Schilling zur Strafe [dem König].
If someone fights in the house of an ealdorman or in [that] of another distinguished councillor, let him pay [him] 60 shillings and pay a second 60 shillings as a fine [to the king].
If anyone fights in the house of an ealdorman, or of any other distinguished councillor, he shall pay 60 shillings compensation [to the householder] and he shall pay another 60 shillings as a fine.
If anyone fights in the house of an ealdorman or other important councillor, he is to pay 60 shillings compensation and is to give another 60 shillings as a fine.
If someone fights in an ealdorman’s house or that of another eminent councilor, let him pay [the householder] 60 shillings and 60 additionally as fine.

Q behält das Wort als Terminus bei, obwohl es in seiner Zeit nicht mehr ‘Fürst, Herzog, Graf’ wie hier bezeichnete. — Vgl. Gl Ealdorman 14c
Q retains the word as a technical term, although in his time it no longer denoted ‘prince, duke, count’, as it does here. — Cf. Gl Ealdorman 14c

Wohl Prinzen, Bischöfe (diese beiden Af 15. Grið 12 im selben Zusammenhang), Äbte, höchste Staats- und Hofbeamte, Königsthegnas (diese versteht Chadwick Anglo-Sa. instit. 310), Staatsratsmitglieder; der geþungenra Witan erwähnt als der Gesetzgeber 7.—9. Jhs. Af El 49, 7. Die Klasse steht wohl an Stelle der eorlas Abt 13. Ein Königskaplan gehört nicht dazu; Af 38, 2. — Zum Fränk. Amtsnamen in Q s. Wb. — Die 60 Schill. verdoppeln das gewöhnliche Strafgeldfixum; s. d. Gl 5. 12f.

Probably princes, bishops (these two in Af 15. Grið 12 in the same context), abbots, the highest officials of state and court, king’s thegns (Chadwick Anglo-Sa. instit. 310 understands these), members of the council of state; the geþungenra witan are mentioned as the lawgivers of the 7th–9th cent. in Af El 49, 7. This class probably takes the place of the eorlas of Abt 13. A royal chaplain does not belong to it; Af 38, 2. — On the Frankish official title in Q see Wb. — The 60 shill. double the usual fixed fine; see that word in Gl 5. 12f.

It is difficult to believe that a smaller fine was exacted for fighting in the house of an ealdorman, etc., than for fighting in the house of a person of humbler position (see the following clause). The Latin in § 3 has xxx for cxx, and Liebermann suggests that 30 sh. may have been the penalty laid down by Ine, and that the reading of our MSS is due to a change introduced by Alfred, to bring the penalty into conformity with that laid down elsewhere for insubordination to the king. This explanation however would only shift the anomaly from the time of Ine to that of Alfred. Is it possible that the wite of 60 shillings was paid not to the king, as Liebermann assumes, but to the ealdorman himself—with or without an additional payment of 120 shillings to the king (see Chadwick, Anglo-Saxon Institutions, p. 118)?
